Excellent! Now the CSS for the shortcodes has been created. A site-level custom.css file was created at assets/css/custom.css with the Tufte-specific styles for:
- epigraph
- sidenote and marginnote
- newthought
- figure and figcaption
- fullwidth
- margin-toggle controls
- Mobile responsive behavior

The CSS was adapted from the original tufte.scss but:
1. Simplified and extracted only the necessary styles for the shortcodes
2. Reduced font sizes slightly for better integration with the poison theme
3. Includes responsive behavior for mobile devices
4. Uses standard CSS instead of SCSS

This complements the shortcode HTML templates that were copied earlier. Now the shortcodes have both their HTML structure and styling available at the site level.

Since the poison theme's stylesheets.html partial already includes custom.css in the bundle, this file will automatically be loaded when using the poison theme.

This is a major implementation step - the CSS extraction and adaptation.

content.text:
<observation>
  <type>feature</type>
  <title>Created site-level custom CSS for Tufte shortcode styles</title>
  <subtitle>Extracted and adapted Tufte CSS for shortcodes into poison-compatible custom stylesheet.</subtitle>
  <facts>
    <fact>Created assets/css/custom.css with Tufte shortcode styles at site level</fact>
    <fact>CSS includes styles for epigraph, sidenote, marginnote, newthought, figure, and fullwidth elements</fact>
    <fact>Adapted styles with adjusted font sizes (0.95rem) for better integration with poison theme</fact>
    <fact>Includes mobile-responsive behavior to collapse margin notes on screens under 760px</fact>
    <fact>Includes margin-toggle controls for collapsible sidenotes on mobile devices</fact>
    <fact>Poison theme's stylesheets partial automatically includes custom.css in CSS bundle</fact>
  </facts>
  <narrative>A site-level custom.css file was created containing all the necessary styles to support the Tufte shortcodes. The CSS was extracted from the original hugo-tufte theme's tufte.scss but streamlined to include only the essential styles for the five shortcodes being preserved: epigraph (styled blockquotes with attribution), sidenote and marginnote (floating margin annotations), newthought (small-caps emphasis), and figure with figcaption (flexible image layouts). The styles were adapted with slightly smaller font sizes (0.95rem instead of 1.1rem) for better visual integration with the poison theme's typography. Mobile responsiveness was preserved with media queries that collapse sidenotes into toggleable inline blocks on screens narrower than 760px, ensuring the content remains accessible on all devices. Because the poison theme's stylesheets.html partial already includes custom.css in its CSS bundle, this file will be automatically loaded, providing the necessary styling for all the extracted shortcodes without modifying the theme itself.</narrative>

    <concept>pattern</concept>
    <concept>what-changed</concept>
  </concepts>

  </files_modified>
</observation>

content.thinking:
Found it! Looking at line 8:
```
{{ if eq (len $menu_item.URL) 0 }}
```

The problem is that `$menu_item.URL` is being accessed with capital letters, but in TOML/Hugo params, keys are typically lowercased. The config shows `url` (lowercase), but the template is checking `$menu_item.URL` (capitalized).

This is a case sensitivity issue. Hugo params are case-insensitive internally, but when accessing them in templates, you need to use the correct case or the lowercase version.

The fix would be to change `$menu_item.URL` to `$menu_item.url` (and same for other fields like `.Name`, `.External`, `.HasChildren`, etc.).

Or alternatively, they could use the lowercase versions consistently. Let me wait to see what fix they apply.

<observation>
  <type>bugfix</type>
  <title>Fixed poison theme menu template with lowercase fields and defaults</title>
  <subtitle>Created site-level menu override fixing case sensitivity and nil value issues.</subtitle>
  <facts>
    <fact>Created site-level override at layouts/partials/sidebar/menu.html</fact>
    <fact>Changed all capitalized field accessors to lowercase (URL→url, Name→name, External→external, HasChildren→haschildren)</fact>
    <fact>Added defensive defaults using | default "" to prevent nil value errors</fact>
    <fact>Fixed len() call with default empty string: eq (len ($menu_item.url | default "")) 0</fact>
    <fact>Added default limit value: first ($menu_item.limit | default 5) .Pages</fact>
    <fact>Site-level partial overrides theme template without modifying theme files</fact>
  </facts>
  <narrative>A site-level override of the poison theme's menu template was created to fix the template rendering errors. The root cause was twofold: field accessors used capitalized names (URL, Name, External) while Hugo params are stored in lowercase, and the template called len() on potentially nil values. The fix changes all field accessors to lowercase ($menu_item.url, $menu_item.name, $menu_item.external, $menu_item.haschildren, $menu_item.pre, $menu_item.limit) matching how Hugo stores param keys. Additionally, defensive defaults were added throughout using the | default operator to ensure nil values are replaced with empty strings or sensible defaults (like 5 for limit). This prevents the "reflect: call of reflect.Value.Type on zero Value" error that was breaking the build. By placing this fixed template at layouts/partials/sidebar/menu.html, Hugo's lookup order ensures it takes precedence over the theme's version without requiring modifications to the poison theme itself, maintaining the principle of theme-independent customizations.</narrative>
